title: Ethics, Independence & Professional Conduct
objectives: Distinguish independence of mind and appearance from objectivity.
Apply the appropriate AICPA, SEC/PCAOB, GAO, or DOL independence requirements.
Respond to financial-interest, management-participation, and confidentiality threats.

title: Skepticism, Judgment & Audit Responsibilities
objectives: Evaluate contradictory evidence without assuming dishonesty or unquestioning trust.
Distinguish management’s responsibilities from the auditor’s reasonable-assurance objective.
Recognize fraud incentives, judgment biases, and appropriate escalation.

title: Engagement Scope, Acceptance & Written Terms
objectives: Match assurance levels to audits, reviews, compilations, preparations, and agreed-upon procedures.
Evaluate engagement preconditions and predecessor communications.
Document responsibilities and evaluate requests to change engagement type.

title: Documentation, Governance Communication & Quality
objectives: Prepare documentation understandable to an experienced auditor with no prior engagement connection.
Distinguish significant deficiencies from material weaknesses and appropriate communication.
Apply engagement quality responsibilities, consultation, and supervision.

title: Understand the Entity & Design the Audit Strategy
objectives: Connect business conditions to assertion-level risks.
Distinguish inherent, control, detection, and audit risk.
Adjust the nature, timing, and extent of audit work.

title: Internal Controls, Walkthroughs & Service Organizations
objectives: Apply COSO components and control design concepts.
Distinguish design, implementation, and operating effectiveness.
Use SOC reports and identify complementary user-entity controls.

title: Materiality, Fraud & Planned Responses
objectives: Calculate materiality using specified benchmarks and evaluate qualitative factors.
Distinguish overall materiality, performance materiality, and clearly trivial thresholds.
Design responses to fraud risks and aggregated misstatements.

title: Specialists, Related Parties & Specialized Engagement Risks
objectives: Evaluate specialists and internal auditors without transferring responsibility.
Respond to related parties, estimates, and noncompliance risks.
Identify additional considerations in single audits and employee-benefit-plan audits.

title: Assertions & Direction of Testing
objectives: Translate an assertion into a specific possible misstatement.
Choose the correct population and direction of testing.
Distinguish tests of controls from substantive procedures.

title: Sampling, Projection & Evaluation of Exceptions
objectives: Choose attribute or variables sampling to match the objective.
Distinguish sampling risk from execution errors.
Evaluate deviations and projected misstatements with sampling uncertainty.

title: Data Reliability & Analytical Procedures
objectives: Validate completeness, accuracy, and relevance of data before analysis.
Build an independent and sufficiently precise expectation.
Investigate significant differences rather than accepting unsupported explanations.

title: Confirmations, Cash, Receivables & Inventory
objectives: Evaluate evidence relevance and reliability in context.
Maintain control over confirmation requests and responses.
Select appropriate inventory observation and alternative procedures.

title: Liabilities, Estimates, Litigation & Related Parties
objectives: Search for unrecorded liabilities using appropriate source evidence.
Evaluate estimation uncertainty and management bias.
Obtain evidence about litigation and significant unusual transactions.

title: Investments, Fair Value & Evidence Conclusions
objectives: Audit ownership, valuation, and disclosure of investments.
Evaluate contradictory evidence and fair-value inputs.
Determine whether evidence is sufficient and appropriate for a conclusion.

title: Unmodified, Qualified, Adverse & Disclaimer Opinions
objectives: Distinguish known misstatement from insufficient evidence.
Evaluate materiality and pervasiveness in opinion decisions.
Explain why an emphasis paragraph cannot cure a modified-opinion issue.

title: Subsequent Events, Going Concern & Written Representations
objectives: Evaluate evidence arising after the reporting date.
Assess going-concern disclosures and management plans.
Understand the role and timing of written representations.

title: Report Elements, CAMs, KAMs & Comparative Information
objectives: Recognize the function of opinion, basis, responsibility, and other report sections.
Distinguish critical/key audit matters from modifications.
Evaluate comparative reporting and special-purpose frameworks.

title: Reviews, Compilations, Attestation & Compliance Reporting
objectives: Compare assurance and reporting across service types.
Respond to evidence of misstatement during a review.
Understand appropriate scope and use of attestation and compliance reports.

title: Tax Practitioner Duties & Return Positions
objectives: Apply diligence and competence to tax preparation and advice.
Evaluate support and disclosure for return positions.
Distinguish professional discipline from tax penalties.

title: IRS Examinations, Appeals, Courts & Penalties
objectives: Distinguish administrative review and judicial forums.
Apply specified assessment periods and penalty facts.
Identify documentation needed to support tax treatment.

title: Tax Authority, Liability, Confidentiality & Privilege
objectives: Evaluate authoritative sources and jurisdiction.
Distinguish confidentiality from legal privilege.
Recognize professional duties to clients and third parties.

title: Contracts, Agency, Performance & Remedies
objectives: Identify contract formation and enforceability issues.
Distinguish actual authority, apparent authority, and ratification.
Apply breach, discharge, and remedy principles.

title: Secured Transactions, Creditors & Bankruptcy
objectives: Distinguish attachment, perfection, and priority.
Apply ordinary debtor, creditor, and guarantor principles.
Recognize the automatic stay and bankruptcy-discharge limitations.

title: Business Entities, Owner Duties & Federal Regulation
objectives: Compare legal liability and management characteristics of common entities.
Evaluate worker classification and employment obligations.
Recognize anti-bribery and other business compliance issues.

title: Tax Basis: Purchases, Gifts, Inheritances & Conversion
objectives: Compute acquisition and adjusted basis.
Apply the different gain/loss basis rules for gifts.
Distinguish inherited basis and conversion depreciation basis.

title: Depreciation, Expensing & Capitalization
objectives: Apply cost-recovery assumptions in the proper order.
Distinguish capital improvements from current expenditures.
Track tax-law periods, conventions, and limits.

title: Realized Gain, Recognized Gain & Character
objectives: Compute amount realized and adjusted-basis gain or loss.
Distinguish capital assets and business property.
Evaluate depreciation recapture using stated facts.

title: Gross Income, Exclusions & Investment Income
objectives: Identify taxable receipts and common exclusions.
Compute capital gains using basis and holding-period facts.
Distinguish receipt of an asset from its later disposition.

title: AGI, Itemized Deductions & Taxable Income
objectives: Distinguish adjustments to income from deductions after AGI.
Compare allowed itemized deductions with the applicable standard deduction.
Apply supplied limitations and compute taxable income.

title: Filing Status, Credits, Payments & Return Review
objectives: Identify filing-status facts and related responsibilities.
Apply refundable and nonrefundable credit mechanics.
Reconcile total tax, withholding, estimates, and refunds.

title: C Corporations: Taxable Income, Formation & Distributions
objectives: Reconcile book income to taxable income using stated tax adjustments.
Identify basic Section 351 formation requirements.
Distinguish dividends, basis recovery, and capital gain.

title: Partnership Income, Outside Basis & Distributions
objectives: Distinguish partnership ordinary income and separately stated items.

title: S Corporations: Eligibility, Basis & Pass-Through Items
objectives: Recognize core S-election eligibility requirements.
Distinguish stock basis, direct debt basis, and guarantees.

title: Financial Ratios, Trends & Data Quality
objectives: Compute and interpret liquidity, profitability, and turnover measures.
Distinguish operating changes from accounting or data changes.
Use reliable comparable data for business conclusions.

title: Budgets, Forecasts, Cash Planning & Working Capital
objectives: Build operating and cash budgets from linked assumptions.
Distinguish forecasts from hypothetical projections.
Evaluate the cash consequences of collection and payment timing.

title: Cost Behavior, CVP & Relevant Decisions
objectives: Compute contribution margin and break-even output.
Distinguish relevant, sunk, and opportunity costs.
Evaluate constrained-resource and make-or-buy choices.

title: Standard Costs, Variances & Performance Interpretation
objectives: Compute price/rate and quantity/efficiency variances.

Investigate causes and avoid evaluating managers from one variance alone.

title: Capital Structure, Cost of Capital & Investment Decisions
objectives: Compute weighted cost of capital from specified assumptions.
Evaluate discounted cash flows and opportunity costs.
Distinguish NPV, payback, and accounting return measures.

title: Performance Measures, Enterprise Risk & Valuation
objectives: Combine financial and nonfinancial performance evidence.
Connect enterprise risk to strategy and objectives.
Apply supplied valuation multiples and economic relationships.

title: Revenue Contracts, Modifications & Principal–Agent Analysis
objectives: Allocate transaction price to distinct performance obligations.
Evaluate modification and variable-consideration facts.
Distinguish principal and agent presentation.

title: Lessor Accounting & Lessee Measurement Review
objectives: Apply lease classification and present-value measurement facts.
Compute a lessor’s investment and interest under supplied assumptions.
Review a lessee’s liability and right-of-use asset.

title: Business Combinations, Goodwill & Noncontrolling Interests
objectives: Apply the acquisition method to specified fair values.
